beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Californium?
beginner.explanation: Californium-252 splits on its own and releases neutrons. A tiny sealed source is used in research and in some mining and medical instruments.

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Californium?
beginner.explanation: Californium is built up by a long chain of neutron captures, starting from plutonium or curium. Only specialized reactors make it.

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Californium?

beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Californium?
options: In December 1898, months after polonium, Marie and Pierre Curie announced a second, far more radioactive element in pitchblende.
André-Louis Debierne, a colleague of the Curies, found a new radioactive substance in pitchblende residues in 1899 and named it actinium, from the Greek aktis, a ray.
Thompson, Kenneth Street, Ghiorso, and Seaborg made element 98 in 1950 by bombarding curium with alpha particles.
Marguerite Perey, working at the Curie Institute, found a short-lived alkali metal among the decay products of actinium in 1939.
beginner.explanation: Thompson, Kenneth Street, Ghiorso, and Seaborg made element 98 in 1950 by bombarding curium with alpha particles.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Californium?
options: André-Louis Debierne examined the rare-earth fraction of pitchblende after uranium, polonium, and radium had been removed.
Thompson, Kenneth Street, Ghiorso, and Seaborg repeated the helium-ion experiment on a curium target in 1950.
Marguerite Perey followed the decay products of actinium-227 at the Curie Institute.
After polonium had been traced into the bismuth fraction of pitchblende, Marie and Pierre Curie found a second excess of activity in the barium fraction.
beginner.explanation: Thompson, Kenneth Street, Ghiorso, and Seaborg repeated the helium-ion experiment on a curium target in 1950.
